low_band_rows.uncertainty_ground: The literary function of the book's opening shifting reference -- enallage (3ms 'let him kiss me' turning to 2ms address inside MT 1:2) versus an unmarked chorus intrusion at the 1cp 'we will be glad' of MT 1:4 -- is argued rather than settled by any tier-1 form; bakh (oshb:Song.1.4, byte tier) is 2fs in form and 2ms only on a pausal reading, left unsettled with no morphology layer staged.

The closing seam is carried by bracket completion rather than by a voice-shift marker, and the woman's first-person run that begins inside MT 2:3 is severed by the cut; the re-cut remedy is unavailable at verse granularity, so the severed run stands as a disclosure. Boss ruling forbids raising confidence on the strength of the bracket warrant.

The verse's speaker is genuinely unmarked by any tier-1 form in the staged extract: no gender on the plural imperative, no dodi/rayati anchor, no daughters-of-Jerusalem vocative. The row states explicitly that the ISOLATION itself, not any single wrong guess about who speaks it, is what the bytes cannot settle.

unit_type is a closest-fit application, not a form match: MT 3:6-3:10 is third-person processional description rather than direct address, and the only addressee shift (to the daughters of Zion) surfaces at the closing imperative in MT 3:11.

A transitional single verse issuing an invitation that only its own reply can settle, and that reply falls in the following verse, which is argued separately on its own bytes -- so the unit's function depends on material outside its span.

The praise frame is contested and the internal MT 6:7|6:8 join carries no marked seam, which the row's confidence reflects rather than resolves; the wider span past the mechanically derived body-part run (MT 6:5-6:7) rests on the byte-tier ayumah inclusio plus the absence of address forms at MT 6:8-6:10.

MT 6:12 is the merkavot-ammi-nadiv crux, the book's hardest line: the speaker's identity and the syntax of nafshi-samatni are held open rather than decided, and the OSHB exegesis note there is single-witness apparatus, not a text-level seam.

Two distinct holds on one verse: the dance-of-Mahanaim construal is held open, and the voice assignment of the mah-tehezu clause is held open between the 1cp form ve-nehezeh bakh with its 2fs suffix and the 2mp form tehezu in the same clause -- weighed on both sides without deciding. This is the offset-zone seam verse (MT 7:1 = WEB 6:13).

MT 8:6 shalhevet-yah is a classic construal crux (intensive 'mighty flame' versus divine element) held rather than decided with the OSHB divided-token fact disclosed; the merged 8:5-8:7 frame is itself contested, and MT 8:5 carries an intra-verse turn from 3fs question to 1cs/2ms address disclosed rather than resolved.
